Chapter XIV.—That Out of the
Children of the Night and of the Darkness, Children of the Light
and of the Day are Made.

15. And so say I too, O my God, where art
Thou? Behold where Thou art! In Thee I breathe a little, when I
pour out my soul by myself in the voice of joy and praise, the
sound of him that keeps holy-day.<ref>
''Ibid.'' ver. 4.</ref> And yet it is “cast down,”
because it relapses and becomes a deep, or rather it feels that it
is still a deep. Unto it doth my faith speak which Thou hast
kindled to enlighten my feet in the night, “Why art thou cast
down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted in me? hope thou in
God;”<ref>
''Ibid.'' ver. 5.</ref> His
“word is a lamp unto my feet.”<ref>
Ps. cxix. 105.</ref> Hope and endure until the
night,—the mother of the wicked,—until the anger of the Lord be
overpast,<ref>
Job xiv. 13.</ref> whereof we
also were once children who were sometimes darkness,<ref>
Eph. ii. 3, and v. 8.</ref> the
remains whereof we carry about us in our body, dead on account of
sin,<ref>
Rom. viii. 10.</ref> “until
the day break and the shadows flee away.”<ref>
Cant. ii. 17.</ref> “Hope thou in the Lord.” In
the morning I shall stand in Thy presence, and contemplate Thee;<ref>
Ps. v. 3.</ref> I shall
for ever confess unto Thee.<ref>
Ps. xxx. 12.</ref> In the morning I shall stand in
Thy presence, and shall see “the health of my countenance,”<ref>
Ps. xliii. 5.</ref> my God,
who also shall quicken our mortal bodies by the Spirit that
dwelleth in us,<ref>
Rom. viii. 11.</ref> because in
mercy He was borne over our inner darksome and floating deep.
Whence we have in this pilgrimage received “an earnest”<ref>
2 Cor. i. 22.</ref> that we
should now be light, whilst as yet we “are saved by hope,”<ref>
Rom. viii. 24.</ref> and are
the children of light, and the children of the day,—not the
children of the night nor of the darkness,<ref>
Though ''of'' the light, we are not yet 
''in'' the light; and though, in this grey dawn of the coming day,
we have a foretaste of the vision that shall be, we cannot hope, as
he says ''in'' ''Ps.'' v. 4, to “see Him as He is” until
the darkness of sin be overpast.</ref> which yet we have been.<ref>
Eph. v. 8,
and 1 Thess. v. 5.</ref> Betwixt
whom and us, in this as yet uncertain state of human knowledge,
Thou only dividest, who provest our hearts<ref>
Ps. vii. 9.</ref> and callest the light day, and the
darkness night.<ref>
Gen. i. 5.</ref> For who
discerneth us but Thou? But what have we that we have not received
of Thee?<ref>
1 Cor. iv. 7.</ref> Out of the
same lump vessels unto honour, of which others also are made to
dishonour.<ref>
Rom. ix. 21.</ref>
